problem: The brush diameter d is introduced but then the sentence says the brush stamps colour into every pixel its path touches, which describes a zero-width path and leaves d unused. A brush of diameter d covers a disc of pixels around the path.
fix: A brush of diameter d stamps colour into every pixel within d/2 of the path it follows, so a soft edge is a band of partly transparent pixels.

problem: The sentence "Its corner radius cannot be changed afterwards" is confusing for ellipses and text, which have no corner radius at all, and it hides the general point that painted shapes cannot be re-edited.
fix: Any shape drawn in a paint program is rendered into the bitmap the moment you release the mouse, so its geometry can no longer be re-edited; for a rectangle, even the corner radius is fixed.

problem: "Resampling throws pixels away and does change it" is true only for downsampling. Upsampling creates new pixels and also changes the byte count, so the trap as written can make a student think all resampling reduces size.
fix: Resampling changes the pixel count: downsampling throws pixels away and reduces the size, while upsampling adds pixels and increases it. Resize alone changes only the dpi and print size.

problem: "24-bit RGB and 8-bit indexed both hold one byte per channel or per palette index" is ambiguous: a 24-bit RGB pixel is 3 bytes, while an 8-bit indexed pixel is 1 byte. A student may take away the wrong byte count.
fix: 24-bit RGB uses 3 bytes per pixel (one byte for each of the R, G and B channels) and 8-bit indexed uses 1 byte per pixel (one palette index), but the indexed image is limited to 256 colours.

problem: "The third changes the whole bitmap at once" conflicts with the table's own example, crop, which keeps part of the bitmap and discards the rest rather than changing the whole image.
fix: The third family works on the pixel image, often on a selected region of it — crop, resample, tone and hue.
